passages.note: Senate roll call 520 on HB 1447's Conference Committee Report; Donato voted Yea, but the enrolled bill bundles multiple unrelated education matters.
The bill-details digest describes only the third-party-vendor-survey provision, not the school-library section; shows Donato as Senate sponsor.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Stacey Donato, Sen. Jeff Raatz.

passages.provision_quote: (2) procedure for each school to allow a: (A) parent or guardian of a student enrolled in the school; or (B) community member: (i) within the school district; or (ii) within the school district in which the charter school is located; to submit a request to remove material from the school library that is obscene (as described in IC 35-49-2-1) or harmful to minors (as described in IC 35-49-2-2); and (3) response and appeal procedure for each school to respond to a removal request submitted by a parent, guardian, or community member described in subdivision (2). (b) The response and appeal procedure established under subsection (a)(3) must require the governing body to review the request at the next public meeting.
passages.note: Enrolled Act text of the new IC 20-26-5.5 school-library chapter, enacted by the same Conference Committee Report Donato voted on.

rows.reasoning: HB 1447 (2023)'s Conference Committee Report bundles student-survey privacy, patriotic-observance/political-neutrality rules, obscenity-dissemination amendments, and the new school-library chapter (IC 20-26-5.5) into a single vote, so Donato's Yea on Roll Call 520 is multi-subject and cannot alone establish a library-books rung. The enacted library provision lets a parent or community member request removal of material that is 'obscene' or 'harmful to minors,' reviewed and appealed to 'the governing body' at its next public meeting -- a restrictive direction, but it names neither rung 3's review committee of educators and parents, rung 4's interim pull, nor rung 5's no-review report standard, so it is direction-only. Her sponsorship record is tied to the bill's survey-privacy digest only, not the library section, so it is off-question here.
